newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CVRD slips on sell-off flak.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CVRD slips on sell-off flak.

text.p: Brazilian state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce's blue-chip preferred shares slipped 0.89 percent in the morning on worries about mounting opposition to government plans to privatize the firm, market sources said.
Two former Brazilian presidents, Senate chief Jose Sarney and Itamar Franco, have joined forces in opposing Vale's sell-off, slated to begin in February.
The company's preferred stock traded at 21.15 reais at 1230 local time/1430 GMT in thin trade, down from Tuesday's close at 21.34 percent.

Analysts do not see the sell-off as seriously threatened at this point because of the potentially devastating impact on the market and on the credibility of Cardoso's economic program if he gives in on this issue.
"It would be terrible. It would be a step back to the past," Missima said. "If Cardoso goes back on Vale, it means he could also go back on telecoms, energy. It would be a disaster."
However, keeping CVRD's privatization on track "will depend on the political ability of Fernando Henrique Cardoso to handle the situation," Missima said.
Vale's common voting shares were up 0.39 percent at 25.50 reais, but most traders and analysts said the move was meaningless as volume was next to nil, brokers said.
"There are concerns about this Sarney-Itamar alliance," said Sergio Missima of Fator Securities in Brazil.
Missima, an analyst, said some investors are concerned about the increasing conflict over the sell-off, while others are simply taking advantage of the worries to force the price down.

Franco's opposition to Vale's privatization appears to be based on genuine nationalism, but Sarney is merely trying to gain concessions from President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on other issues, market sources said.
"It's the same political junk as usual," a trader said.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 248 5413 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
